audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for spiritual gifts, one Spirit/many gifts, one body/many members, weaker members honored, gifts ranked toward love in chapter 13.

verses.restored: Now concerning spiritual things/gifts, siblings, I do not want you to be unaware.

familiar.text: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant.

modern.text: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.

original.text: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν.

verses.restored: You know that when you were nations, you were being led away to voiceless idols, however you were led.

familiar.text: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.

modern.text: You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.

original.text: οἴδατε ὅτι ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι.

verses.restored: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in Spirit of the Divine says, Jesus is accursed; and no one is able to say, Jesus is Lord, except in holy Spirit.

familiar.text: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.

original.text: διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐν πνεύματι θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει· Ἀνάθεμα ⸀Ἰησοῦς, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν· ⸂Κύριος Ἰησοῦς⸃ εἰ μὴ ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.

verses.restored: There are varieties of grace-gifts, but the same Spirit;

familiar.text: Now there are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.

modern.text: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.

original.text: Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα·

verses.restored: and there are varieties of services, but the same Lord;

familiar.text: And there are differences of administrations, but the same Lord.

modern.text: There are different ministries, but the same Lord.

original.text: καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς κύριος·

verses.restored: and there are varieties of workings, but the same Divine, the One working all things in all.

familiar.text: And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all.

modern.text: There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.

original.text: καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ⸂ὁ δὲ⸃ ⸀αὐτὸς θεός, ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.

verses.restored: To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit toward what benefits.

familiar.text: But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.

modern.text: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.

original.text: ἑκάστῳ δὲ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον.

verses.restored: For to one through the Spirit is given word of wisdom, and to another word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,

familiar.text: For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit;

modern.text: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

original.text: ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα,

verses.restored: to another trust in the same Spirit, to another grace-gifts of healings in the one Spirit,

familiar.text: To another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit;

modern.text: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,

original.text: ⸀ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πνεύματι, ⸀ἄλλῳ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ⸀ἑνὶ πνεύματι,

verses.restored: to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another discernings of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues.

familiar.text: To another the working of miracles; to another prophecy; to another discerning of spirits; to another divers kinds of tongues; to another the interpretation of tongues:

modern.text: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

original.text: ⸀ἄλλῳ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων, ⸁ἄλλῳ προφητεία, ⸀1ἄλλῳ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων, ⸀ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν, ⸀2ἄλλῳ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν·

verses.restored: But all these things the one and same Spirit works, distributing to each individually just as he wills.

familiar.text: But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.

modern.text: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines. The Body of Christ

original.text: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται.

verses.restored: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, being many, are one body, so also Messiah.

familiar.text: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.

modern.text: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.

original.text: Καθάπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ἕν ἐστιν καὶ μέλη ⸂πολλὰ ἔχει⸃, πάντα δὲ τὰ μέλη τοῦ ⸀σώματος πολλὰ ὄντα ἕν ἐστιν σῶμα, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός·

verses.restored: For in one Spirit we all were baptized into one body, whether Judeans or Greeks, whether enslaved or free, and all were given one Spirit to drink.

familiar.text: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free; and have been all made to drink into one Spirit.

modern.text: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.

original.text: καὶ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ πνεύματι ἡμεῖς πάντες εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν, εἴτε Ἰουδαῖοι εἴτε Ἕλληνες, εἴτε δοῦλοι εἴτε ἐλεύθεροι, καὶ ⸀πάντες ἓν πνεῦμα ἐποτίσθημεν.

verses.restored: For the body also is not one member but many.

familiar.text: For the body is not one member, but many.

modern.text: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.

original.text: Καὶ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα οὐκ ἔστιν ἓν μέλος ἀλλὰ πολλά.

verses.restored: If the foot should say, Because I am not a hand, I am not from the body, not because of this is it not from the body.

familiar.text: If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

modern.text: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

original.text: ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὁ πούς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ χείρ, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος;

verses.restored: And if the ear should say, Because I am not an eye, I am not from the body, not because of this is it not from the body.

familiar.text: And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?

modern.text: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν εἴπῃ τὸ οὖς· Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὀφθαλμός, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος·

verses.restored: If the whole body were eye, where would hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would smell be?

familiar.text: If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling?

modern.text: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?

original.text: εἰ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ὀφθαλμός, ποῦ ἡ ἀκοή; εἰ ὅλον ἀκοή, ποῦ ἡ ὄσφρησις;

verses.restored: But now the Divine placed the members, each one of them, in the body just as he willed.

familiar.text: But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.

modern.text: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.

original.text: ⸀νυνὶ δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἔθετο τὰ μέλη, ἓν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν, ἐν τῷ σώματι καθὼς ἠθέλησεν.

verses.restored: If all were one member, where would the body be?

familiar.text: And if they were all one member, where were the body?

modern.text: If they were all one part, where would the body be?

original.text: εἰ δὲ ἦν τὰ πάντα ἓν μέλος, ποῦ τὸ σῶμα;

verses.restored: But now many members, yet one body.

familiar.text: But now are they many members, yet but one body.

modern.text: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

original.text: νῦν δὲ πολλὰ ⸀μὲν μέλη, ἓν δὲ σῶμα.

verses.restored: The eye is not able to say to the hand, I have no need of you; or again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

familiar.text: And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.

modern.text: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

original.text: οὐ δύναται δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί· Χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω, ἢ πάλιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῖς ποσίν· Χρείαν ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔχω·

verses.restored: But much more, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are necessary,

familiar.text: Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary:

modern.text: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

original.text: ἀλλὰ πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὰ δοκοῦντα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενέστερα ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖά ἐστιν,

verses.restored: and those we think to be less honorable in the body, these we clothe with more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant presentability,

familiar.text: And those members of the body, which we think to be less honourable, upon these we bestow more abundant honour; and our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness.

modern.text: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,

original.text: καὶ ἃ δοκοῦμεν ἀτιμότερα εἶναι τοῦ σώματος, τούτοις τιμὴν περισσοτέραν περιτίθεμεν, καὶ τὰ ἀσχήμονα ἡμῶν εὐσχημοσύνην περισσοτέραν ἔχει,

verses.restored: but our presentable parts have no need. But the Divine blended the body together, giving more abundant honor to the one lacking,

familiar.text: For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked:

modern.text: whereas our presentable parts have no such need. But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,

original.text: τὰ δὲ εὐσχήμονα ἡμῶν οὐ χρείαν ⸀ἔχει. ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς συνεκέρασεν τὸ σῶμα, τῷ ⸀ὑστεροῦντι περισσοτέραν δοὺς τιμήν,

verses.restored: so that there may be no split in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.

familiar.text: That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.

modern.text: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.

original.text: ἵνα μὴ ᾖ ⸀σχίσμα ἐν τῷ σώματι, ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσι τὰ μέλη.

verses.restored: And if one member suffers, all the members suffer together; if one member is glorified, all the members rejoice together.

familiar.text: And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it.

modern.text: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. The Greater Gifts

original.text: καὶ ⸀εἴτε πάσχει ἓν μέλος, συμπάσχει πάντα τὰ μέλη· εἴτε δοξάζεται ⸀μέλος, συγχαίρει πάντα τὰ μέλη.

verses.restored: Now you are body of Messiah and members from a part.

familiar.text: Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.

modern.text: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.

original.text: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἐστε σῶμα Χριστοῦ καὶ μέλη ἐκ μέρους.

verses.restored: And the Divine placed some in the assembly: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then grace-gifts of healings, helps, guidances, kinds of tongues.

familiar.text: And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.

modern.text: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.

original.text: καὶ οὓς μὲν ἔθετο ὁ θεὸς ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρῶτον ἀποστόλους, δεύτερον προφήτας, τρίτον διδασκάλους, ἔπειτα δυνάμεις, ⸀ἔπειτα χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων, ἀντιλήμψεις, κυβερνήσεις, γένη γλωσσῶν.

verses.restored: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all powers?

familiar.text: Are all apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? are all workers of miracles?

modern.text: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?

original.text: μὴ πάντες ἀπόστολοι; μὴ πάντες προφῆται; μὴ πάντες διδάσκαλοι; μὴ πάντες δυνάμεις;

verses.restored: Do all have grace-gifts of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?

familiar.text: Have all the gifts of healing? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?

modern.text: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?

original.text: μὴ πάντες χαρίσματα ἔχουσιν ἰαμάτων; μὴ πάντες γλώσσαις λαλοῦσιν; μὴ πάντες διερμηνεύουσιν;

verses.restored: But desire the greater grace-gifts. And still I show you a way beyond measure.

familiar.text: But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.

modern.text: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.

original.text: ζηλοῦτε δὲ τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ ⸀μείζονα. καὶ ἔτι καθʼ ὑπερβολὴν ὁδὸν ὑμῖν δείκνυμι.

translation_notes: Pneumatika in verse 1 may mean spiritual things or spiritual gifts; restored wording keeps both.
The body section is anti-hierarchy medicine: weaker-seeming members are necessary and receive more abundant honor.
